\chapter{Chapter06 — Bent Dual}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter06.Constructions.BentDual}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Double Fourier transform]
\lean{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_vectorFourierCoeff}
\label{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_vectorFourierCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binarySign, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_expect, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_apply, FABL.vector_fourier_expansion, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, every function $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and every
$x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, applying the Fourier transform twice gives $2^{-n}f(x)$ at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Scaled Fourier coefficient function]
\lean{FABL.bentDual}
\label{FABL.bentDual}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff}
For a function $f:(\mathbb F_2)^n\to\mathbb R$, define its bent dual at
$\gamma\in(\mathbb F_2)^n$ to be $2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ times the vector Fourier
coefficient of $f$ at $\gamma$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The dual is sign-valued]
\lean{FABL.IsBent.isSignValued_bentDual}
\label{FABL.IsBent.isSignValued_bentDual}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsBent, FABL.IsSignValued, FABL.bentDual}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$ be bent. Then its dual function, obtained by
multiplying each Walsh Fourier coefficient of $f$ by $2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, takes
values of absolute value $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of the bent dual]
\lean{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_bentDual}
\label{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_bentDual}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.bentDual, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_const_mul, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_vectorFourierCoeff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\bbr$, and suppose $n$ is even. For
every $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, the vector Fourier coefficient of the bent dual of $f$ at
$x$ equals $2^{-n/2}f(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bentness of the dual]
\lean{FABL.IsSignValued.isBent_bentDual}
\label{FABL.IsSignValued.isBent_bentDual}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsBent, FABL.IsSignValued, FABL.bentDual, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_bentDual}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be even, and let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n	o\bbR$ satisfy $|f(x)|=1$ for every $x$. For each
frequency $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, define the dual function to be $2^{n/2}$ times the corresponding
Fourier coefficient of $f$. Then every Fourier coefficient of this dual function has
absolute value $2^{-n/2}$; that is, the dual function is bent.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bentness and sign-valuedness of the dual]
\lean{FABL.IsBent.bentDual}
\label{FABL.IsBent.bentDual}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsBent, FABL.IsBent.isSignValued_bentDual, FABL.IsSignValued, FABL.IsSignValued.isBent_bentDual, FABL.bentDual}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be even, and let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$ be bent and sign-valued, meaning
$|f(x)|=1$ for every $x$. Then its dual function, obtained by multiplying each Walsh
Fourier coefficient of $f$ by $2^{n/2}$, is sign-valued and bent.
\end{theorem}
